prior_importants.description: The scratch runner's fetch drops GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL because it supposedly 'reads no config a session can write'. But it borrows <common>/objects, and a session can plant info/alternates there. During `pup land`'s fetch, git's fetch-pack then starts `git --git-dir=<session repo> for-each-ref`, which reads that repo's config. Before that child starts, git strips GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and GIT_CONFIG_COUNT from its environment, so the `-c` pins and protocol.ext.allow=never are gone, and it has no transport pin either. On Git before 2.44, which ignores GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, a ref there pointing at a missing object triggers a lazy fetch from the session's promisor remote. That fetch runs core.sshCommand (or an allowed file/ftp/helper transport) with the operator's environment.

findings.description: The `RunGitOptions` JSDoc ends "Neither its git nor any git that git starts reads a config a session can write, once it pins `core.alternateRefsCommand`". Coming right after "Only `withScratchGitDir` sets it", it reads as a guarantee of the `reachesRemote` option itself, when it only holds for `withScratchGitDir`'s runner (scratch git dir plus the alternate-refs pin). A future caller could take setting `reachesRemote` as safe for any git. Point to `withScratchGitDir`'s JSDoc, which already states it correctly, instead of repeating the claim here.

`reachesRemote` adds a boolean to the shared `RunGitOptions`, read through a ternary in `spawnOptions`, and it has one setter (`withScratchGitDir`). Put `NO_TRANSPORT_ENV` before `...opts.env` in `spawnOptions` and have `withScratchGitDir` pass `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL: undefined` in its env, which `execFileSync` drops. That removes the field, the ternary and its JSDoc paragraph. Keep the option if you want the opt-out greppable by name.
